# olsrr

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/olsrr)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=olsrr)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/branch/develop/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/rsquaredacademy/olsrr?branch=develop)
<!-- badges: end -->

olsrr helps analysts build and check linear regression models, with tools for diagnostics, variable selection and clear reports.

## Installation

```{r installation, eval = FALSE}
# Release version from CRAN
install.packages("olsrr")

# Development version from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rsquaredacademy/olsrr")
```

## Quick example

```{r setup, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(olsrr)
```

### Read the regression output

Can grocery and detergents-and-paper spending explain milk spending?

```{r regress}
# annual spend of 440 wholesale customers (UCI, CC BY 4.0; see ?wholesale_customers)
model <- lm(milk ~ grocery + detergents_paper, data = wholesale_customers)
ols_regress(model)
```

The two spend variables explain 53.1% of the variation in milk spend.

- Each extra unit of money spent on groceries goes with about 0.62 more units spent on milk.
- Detergents and paper spend adds little once grocery spend is in the model. Its p-value, 0.35, is well above 0.05, so the link could be chance.

### Check the residuals

Are the residuals (the prediction errors) spread evenly, or do they hide a pattern?

```{r resid-fit, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of residuals against fitted milk spend. The residuals spread wider as fitted spend rises."}
ols_plot_resid_fit(model)
```

Residuals are the gaps between actual and predicted milk spend. They fan out as predicted spend rises, so the spread of the errors is not constant.

### Select variables by AIC

Which spend variables belong in the model?

```{r stepwise}
selection <- ols_step_both_aic(
  lm(milk ~ fresh + grocery + frozen + detergents_paper + delicassen, data = wholesale_customers)
)
selection$metrics[, c("step", "variable", "aic", "adj_r2")]
```

The search adds four of the five variables, one per step.

- AIC, a score where lower is better, falls from 8758.8 to 8687.6.
- Adjusted R-squared, the share of variation explained, rises from 0.53 to 0.60.

## Getting help and contributing

**Help:** open an [issue](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/issues) with a minimal reproducible example, built with [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/).

**Contributing:** read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/rsquaredacademy/olsrr/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**Code of Conduct:** Please note that the olsrr project is released with a [Contributor Code of Conduct](https://olsrr.rsquaredacademy.com/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.html). By contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

**Citation:** run `citation("olsrr")`. The [authors page](https://olsrr.rsquaredacademy.com/authors.html) lists the package authors.
